topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Time Minimization
explanation: The memory hierarchy structures storage into levels (e.g., registers, L1, L2, DRAM) ordered by decreasing speed and increasing capacity to mitigate the latency disparity between the CPU and main memory. Caching is the primary mechanism employed to minimize the average memory access time ($T_{avg}$). This is achieved by exploiting the principle of locality of reference, which includes temporal locality (reuse of recently accessed data) and spatial locality (accessing data near recently accessed locations). Active data blocks are moved into faster, lower-latency cache levels closer to the processor. Effective cache management maximizes the cache hit ratio, thereby minimizing the miss penalty and sustaining high CPU throughput.
